subject: Service guarantee appendix: measurement & evidence flow
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@globex.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: measurement and evidence for SLA appendix

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. Procurement and our SRE team are trying to finalize the service guarantee appendix for the contract and we have a couple of specific asks before we move to legal:

- Exactly how you define "uptime" for hosted inference (what endpoints, health-check vs user traffic).
- Latency measurement windows and percentile targets (p50/p95/p99) and how you sample traffic across regions.
- When a credit is triggered, what evidence will you provide? We need a concrete list (raw traces, probe logs, sample request IDs, timeline).
- How do you reconcile synthetic probe failures vs real-customer traffic? We need the weighting rules.

Can you send a mapping that ties each contractual metric to the specific telemetry artifacts you will hand over for audit? Also, procurement would like an expected turnaround time for evidence requests (legal prefers < 5 business days).

Best,
Jane
Jane Doe
Global Procurement, Globex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@globex.com>
Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: 2025-05-22T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: measurement and evidence for SLA appendix

Hi Jane —

Thanks, really helpful list. High-level answers here and I'm attaching a concise "evidence map" that maps each SLA/SLO line item to the telemetry we can provide. Quick summary: 

- Uptime definition: For hosted API we measure "service availability" based on the control-plane and dataplane success rate on the public REST endpoints used by customers (/v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embed). We report a weighted availability metric per region based on successful 2xx responses over total production requests (excluding client-side 4xx). Health-checks are used for internal routing, but they are not the primary contractual signal.

- Latency measurement: We compute p50/p95/p99 on server-side response time from request-accept to final token emission (server processing + model time). Percentiles are computed on a rolling 24h window by default and on contract windows (monthly calendar) for SLA evaluation. We also provide a 1-minute and 5-minute rolling series for on-call debugging.

- Evidence set for crediting: For each incident we can provide: timeline (UTC), raw request ids (up to 1000 sample ids), per-request traces (latency buckets), backend kernel and model version, autoscale/queue metrics, and synthetic probe logs for the same time window. We will redact customer payloads unless a CDA is in place.

- Synthetic vs real traffic: Our standard approach is to correlate synthetic probe signals with sampled production traffic. For credit calculation we weight production traffic at 80% and synthetic probes at 20% by default; we can negotiate different weights or a rule that triggers 100% production-only evaluation if production sampling density crosses a threshold (e.g., >5 requests/sec aggregated over the region during the incident).

Attached: redwood_sla_evidence_map.pdf (mapping + example incident package) and a short SOC2 attestation summary. Turnaround for evidence: we commit to acknowledging requests within 1 business day and delivering a packaged evidence set within 5 business days for standard incidents. For complex multi-region incidents we propose a 10-business-day window (we'll flag those in our initial ack).

I'll loop in our internal SRE and legal reviewers to make sure we can provide the exact artifacts you need without exposing sensitive customer data. Do you have any preferred formats for the evidence bundle (e.g., CSV request list, zipped JSON traces, or a shared Drive folder)?

Regards,
Karthik
Director, Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-23T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: RFP: measurement and evidence for SLA appendix — action items

Laura / Marissa —

Forwarding Globex's questions (below). Procurement wants a concrete evidence map and a signed expectation on turnaround times. Can we align on the following by EOD Friday?

1) Evidence package contents: confirm we can export per-request traces (redacted), list of request ids (CSV), server-side latency histograms, model runtime and kernel build ids, and synthetic probe logs. If any of these need a CDA or special packaging, flag it.

2) Sampling policy: propose we document the sampling fraction we will expose for production traces (default 0.1% of requests, min 100 req/day per region for inclusion). If production sampling is below threshold during an incident, synthetic probes will be used with negotiated weight.

3) Credit calc rule language: propose an incident crediting rule that uses production-only when sample density >= threshold, otherwise blended production+probe with 80/20 weighting. Also include a clause for overlapping incidents (we prorate credits by affected region/time and de-duplicate request ids).

4) Evidence delivery SLA: confirm 1-business-day ack and 5-business-day delivery for single-region incidents; 10 business days for multi-region. Legal wants explicit exclusions for PII and third-party telemetry.

Attaching the draft measurement-playbook-v1.docx and the SLA evidence map. Please comment inline in the playbook; Marissa if you can run the technical feasibility check on sample exports that would be great.

Thanks — I'll plan to send a consolidated reply to Jane Friday afternoon.

—Karthik

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@globex.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: 2025-05-26T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: measurement and evidence for SLA appendix

Karthik —

Appreciate the overview and the attachments. A couple of clarifying items from SRE and legal: 

- For request IDs, can you guarantee monotonic ordering/timestamps so we can reconstruct timelines? Also, please include any sequence ids that map frontend->backend hops.
- For the 0.1% sampling floor: our traffic pattern for one of our apps is bursty (short windows at 200 req/sec). Will the sample policy capture short-lived spikes? If not, we may need a hybrid rule to ensure coverage for high-burst windows.
- If Redwood uses a blended credit during low-sample incidents, how will we see the math in the evidence bundle? We prefer an auditable worksheet that shows inputs (counts, weights, percentiles) and final credit amount.

Finally — procurement flagged SOC2 evidence. The SOC2 attestation summary you attached is helpful, but can you provide a certified SOC2 report or a portal link for compliance review? Our security team needs the report or your audit firm contact.

Next steps: can you include the audit firm contact and a link to the Drive folder where you'll drop the evidence sample for a previous incident (redacted)? We can then loop legal for a narrower redline.

Thanks,
Jane

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@globex.com>
Cc: procurement@globex.com, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-28T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: measurement and evidence for SLA appendix — evidence package and contacts

Jane —

Thanks — great questions, and all addressable. Concrete deliverables from our side: 

1) Evidence package format: CSV for request ids + metadata (timestamp, region, request_id, status_code, latency_ms), gzipped JSON traces for sampled requests, and an "Auditable Worksheet" (spreadsheet) that shows incident inputs and credit math. We'll publish one sample incident package to the shared Drive link below (all payloads redacted).

2) Monotonic timestamps: request ids include server-assigned sequence numbers and RFC3339 timestamps (UTC) so timelines can be reconstructed. We will include mapping keys for frontend->backend hops where available.

3) Sampling for bursty traffic: we'll add a hybrid sampling override — if request rate exceeds 100 req/s sustained for >= 30s, we temporarily increase sampling fraction to capture at least 1% of traffic for that short window. That will be documented in the playbook.

4) Blended math transparency: the Auditable Worksheet will show production_count, probe_count, weights applied, percentile calculations, and the computed credit. We'll also include the raw percentile calculation scripts for independent verification under a CDA.

5) SOC2: we use auditor Brightline LLP. I'll share a limited-access copy of the SOC2 Type II report to your security portal and provide the auditor contact: audit-admin@brightline-llp.com. For procurement, we'll provision the report access within 24 hours of your NDA/CDA signature.

Deliverables/links: 
- Sample incident bundle: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Globex/SLA-Evidence-Map (read-only link will be provided)
- Draft measurement playbook: measurement-playbook-v1.docx (attached)
- Evidence map: redwood_sla_evidence_map.pdf (attached)

I'll ask Laura and Marissa to confirm the feasibility of the hybrid sampling and the export payloads. If Globex can sign the CDA (I've attached a short CDA template) we'll drop the sample SOC2 report into the portal and provide the auditor contact directly.

Proposed timeline: we will send the consolidated playbook and the read-only Drive sample by 2025-06-02, then schedule a technical walkthrough the following week. Please let me know preferred time slots.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_sla_evidence_map.pdf, soc2-attestation-summary.pdf, measurement-playbook-v1.docx
